description:
Zero Budget Natural Farming is an innovative agricultural practice promoted by the Government of India. 

This scheme was officially launched in 2018. 

It aims to reduce the financial burden on farmers by eliminating the need for chemical fertilizers and pesticides. 

The initiative is rooted in the philosophy of sustainable agriculture. 

It emphasizes the use of natural inputs and traditional farming techniques. 

The primary objective of Zero Budget Natural Farming is to make farming economically viable for small and marginal farmers. 

The government aims to increase the income of farmers by reducing their input costs. 

The target is to reach 10 million farmers by 2025. 

This initiative also aims to promote ecological balance and biodiversity. 

The scheme encourages the use of indigenous seeds and natural fertilizers. 

Farmers are trained to use techniques such as mulching and intercropping. 

These methods help in improving soil health and increasing crop yields. 

The government has set a goal to cover 5 million hectares under this farming practice by 2025. 

The benefits of Zero Budget Natural Farming include reduced costs of cultivation. 

Farmers can save up to 50% on their input costs. 

This translates to an average savings of around ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 per hectare annually. 

The scheme also aims to enhance the nutritional quality of food. 

By avoiding chemical inputs, the produce is healthier for consumers. 

Farmers practicing Zero Budget Natural Farming can also access various government support schemes. 

These include the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme. 

Under PM-KISAN, eligible farmers receive ₹6,000 annually in three installments. 

Eligibility for Zero Budget Natural Farming is primarily focused on small and marginal farmers. 

Farmers with landholdings of up to 2 hectares are prioritized. 

There are no specific age limits for participation in this scheme. 

However, farmers must be willing to adopt natural farming practices. 

The application process for Zero Budget Natural Farming involves registration with local agricultural departments. 

Farmers can also register through the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The required documents typically include proof of land ownership and identity verification. 

Farmers may also need to submit a declaration of their willingness to adopt natural farming practices. 

The government conducts training programs and workshops to educate farmers about Zero Budget Natural Farming. 

These sessions are organized at the block and district levels. 

The frequency of these training programs varies based on demand and local agricultural conditions. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of this initiative. 

They are responsible for organizing training sessions and providing resources to farmers. 

The National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management (MANAGE) is involved in capacity building. 

The government has allocated ₹500 crores for promoting Zero Budget Natural Farming in the 2021-22 budget. 

This funding is aimed at supporting research and development in natural farming techniques. 

The scheme also encourages the establishment of farmer producer organizations (FPOs). 

These organizations help farmers in marketing their produce. 

They also provide a platform for sharing knowledge and resources. 

The government has reported that over 1 million farmers have already adopted Zero Budget Natural Farming practices. 

The initiative has been particularly successful in states like Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. 

In Andhra Pradesh, the state government has committed to cover 1 million farmers under this scheme by 2024. 

The state has also launched its own program called the "Rythu Sadhikara Samstha" to support farmers. 

Farmers are encouraged to use local resources and traditional knowledge in their farming practices. 

The scheme promotes the use of cow dung and urine as natural fertilizers. 

These inputs are believed to enhance soil fertility and crop productivity. 

The government also emphasizes the importance of water conservation techniques. 

Farmers are trained in rainwater harvesting and drip irrigation methods. 

These practices help in optimizing water usage and improving crop resilience. 

Zero Budget Natural Farming aligns with the broader goals of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture. 

This mission aims to promote sustainable farming practices across the country. 

The government is also working to create awareness about the benefits of natural farming. 

Various campaigns and outreach programs are conducted to educate farmers. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from farmers who have adopted these practices. 

Many report improved soil health and increased crop yields. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of Zero Budget Natural Farming. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate its impact on farmer incomes. 

The initiative is part of a larger effort to transform Indian agriculture. 

The focus is on making it more sustainable and economically viable. 

Zero Budget Natural Farming is expected to play a significant role in achieving food security. 

It also aims to mitigate the adverse effects of climate change on agriculture. 

The government is committed to expanding this initiative in the coming years. 

This includes increasing funding and resources for training and support. 

The long-term vision is to create a robust ecosystem for natural farming in India. 

This will benefit not only farmers but also consumers and the environment. 

Overall Zero Budget Natural Farming represents a paradigm shift in agricultural practices. 

It encourages a return to traditional methods while leveraging modern knowledge. 

The initiative is crucial for the future of sustainable agriculture in India.
